The answer makes three claims. The first is that the passages do not state which GNN DiffTRe uses. This is a statement about what the passages lack, and it is accurate, since neither passage mentions DiffTRe.

The second claim is that NequIP improves on state-of-the-art accuracy on MD-17 and significantly outperforms invariant GNN interatomic potentials such as SchNet and DimeNet. Passage 010 states both points.

The third claim is that on the revised MD-17 data set the authors report NequIP outperforms all other methods compared. Passage 011 says "only the results on the revised MD-17 data set should be used for comparing... Remarkably, we find that NequIP outperforms all other methods." This follows from the passage.

All claims are supported.
